vocabulary.meaning_en: to give someone credit; admit they did well
vocabulary.note_ar: في الكلام: I gotta hand it to you = I have got to hand it to you
vocabulary.note_en: Spoken: I gotta hand it to you (written: I have got to).
vocabulary.example: I've got to hand it to you; you tried hard.

vocabulary.meaning_en: spoken short form of "have got to"
vocabulary.meaning_ar: صيغة عامية لـ have got to (يجب)
vocabulary.note_ar: للكلام فقط، لا تكتبها في الرسمي
Where are you heading? = إلى أين أنت ذاهب؟
vocabulary.example: She was heading to the store.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to look at someone hard, often in an unfriendly way
vocabulary.example: Why is that man eyeballing me?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to speak rudely, especially to someone in authority
vocabulary.example: Don't mouth off to your father.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to accept and carry a responsibility or burden
vocabulary.example: She shoulders a lot of responsibility at work and at home.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something heavy or difficult you have to carry or deal with
vocabulary.example: Debt can be a heavy burden.

vocabulary.meaning_en: carrying a weapon, like a gun or knife
vocabulary.note_ar: armed to the teeth = مدجّج بالسلاح
vocabulary.note_en: armed to the teeth = with many weapons

vocabulary.meaning_en: to push or hit someone with your elbow to get past
vocabulary.example: He elbowed past the people at the door.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to go in front of people who are waiting in a line
vocabulary.example: Don't butt in line; go to the back.
There was a long queue at the bank.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to punish or hurt someone very badly (used as an exaggeration)
vocabulary.note_ar: تعبير مبالغة للدلالة على ألم أو عقاب شديد
vocabulary.note_en: An exaggeration for extreme pain or punishment.
vocabulary.example: If I break Dad's phone, he'll skin me alive!
Who's footing the bill for dinner?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to accept the truth about a difficult situation
vocabulary.example: It's time to face facts: we need to save money.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to hit someone with your knee
vocabulary.example: He got kneed in the stomach during the football match.

fine_lines.title: head vs elbow vs shoulder (as verbs)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: head = يتّجه. elbow = يدفع بمرفقه ليمرّ. shoulder = يتحمّل مسؤولية.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Head = go in a direction. Elbow = push past with your elbow. Shoulder = carry a responsibility.

examples.sentence: She elbowed her way to the front.

fine_lines.title: foot the bill vs face the facts
fine_lines.explanation_ar: foot the bill = يدفع التكلفة. face the facts = يتقبّل الحقيقة الصعبة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Foot the bill = pay. Face the facts = accept a hard truth.

examples.sentence: The company footed the bill for the trip.
Face the facts: the car is too old to fix.

expressions.phrase: I gotta hand it to you.
expressions.example: I gotta hand it to you; that was a great meal.
Where are you heading? - To the library.

expressions.meaning_en: Why are you staring at me?

expressions.example: Stop mouthing off to your teacher.
Great dinner! Who's footing the bill?

grammar.title: Nouns used as verbs
grammar.explanation_ar: في الإنجليزية يمكن استخدام أسماء أجزاء الجسم كأفعال، وتتغيّر صيغتها مثل أي فعل: head → heading / headed، elbow → elbowed، shoulder → shouldering، foot → footed.
grammar.explanation_en: In English, many body-part nouns can be verbs and change form like normal verbs: head → heading/headed, elbow → elbowed, shoulder → shouldering, foot → footed.
examples: Mr. E was heading to the movies.

questions.question: "One day, Mr. E was ___ to the movies." (going in that direction)
questions.explanation_en: Head to = go in a direction.

questions.question: "Mr. E thought he could ___ in line." (go in front of others)
"Mr. E ___ past them." (pushed with his elbow)
"Other people saw him and ___ him." (stared at him angrily)
questions.explanation_en: Eyeball = stare in an unfriendly way.

questions.question: "He ran away because they were ___." (had weapons)
"It's time to ___ facts. We can't afford a new car."
